chain.label: FAA grandfathered 1968 turboprop STC under 1943 static-only certification basis
chain.trigger: the FAA granted Frakes Aviation the option to use the airplane's original type certificate...instead of requiring Frakes to apply for a new type certificate for the G-73T airplane

chain.label: Wing box fatigue cracks developed undetected over decades with no established fatigue life
chain.trigger: fatigue initiated at the slosh hole because the number of load cycles on the stringer exceeded its fatigue life

caused_by.evidence: there was no existing information for the safe operating life of the G-73T wing structure that could have been used as the basis for inspection and retirement requirements

chain.label: Chalk's Ocean Airways repeatedly applied ineffective/undocumented wing repairs
chain.trigger: many of the repairs were ineffective in that they did not properly restore the load-carrying capability of the wing structure

caused_by.evidence: Sanding marks were observed around the rear Z-stringer slosh hole and fracture lips at right WS 34, suggesting that the sanding was an attempt to remove cracking that had been detected

chain.label: FAA PMI failed to detect and correct deficiencies in Chalk's maintenance program
chain.trigger: the FAA's failure to identify the inadequacy of the Chalk's Ocean Airways maintenance program was causal to the accident

caused_by.evidence: no evidence indicated that the PMI investigated the cause of the repetitive fuel leaks or discussed these issues with company management

chain.label: Fatigue fractures in Z-stringer, skin, and spar cap reached critical length; right wing separated at WS34
chain.trigger: the right wing separated from the accident airplane at WS 34 because of preexisting fatigue fractures and cracks in the rear Z-stringer, lower skin, and rear spar lower spar cap

caused_by.evidence: this multiple-element fatigue damage reduced the residual strength capability of the wing structure and caused the fatigue failure of the wing during normal flight operations
the doubler repair to the accident airplane's lower wing skin at right WS 34 was ineffective because the doublers did not restore the load-carrying capability of the skin
the FAA's failure to identify the inadequacy of the Chalk's Ocean Airways maintenance program was causal to the accident

chain.label: Loss of right wing rendered the airplane uncontrollable
chain.trigger: the right wing separated from the airplane at WS 34 while the airplane was operated within its certificated design envelope, rendering the airplane uncontrollable

caused_by.evidence: there was nothing that the crew could have done to regain control of the airplane after the in-flight separation of the right wing

chain.label: Airplane crashed into shipping channel adjacent to the Port of Miami
chain.trigger: crashed into a shipping channel adjacent to the Port of Miami, Florida, shortly after takeoff from the Miami Seaplane Base

caused_by.evidence: the airplane subsequently descended into the water

chain.label: All 20 people aboard were killed
chain.trigger: All 20 people aboard the airplane were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces
